messages:
incident-bot: Pager alert — P1: elevated 5xx rate for /v1/generate across hosted cluster us-west-2. Triggered 2026-03-14T21:12:00Z. Paging maya (oncall).
maya: ack — I'm on it. Seeing spike in error-rate from 0.2% -> ~12% over last 3m. Customers reporting timeouts + 502s. Will collect traces and logs, tagging SRE.
sam: @maya jumping in. Can you post the top failing route + example request id? I'll start looking at ingress and upstream.
maya: top route: /v1/generate, sample req id: req_20260314_3178. Failing status mostly 502/504 from proxy -> runtime nodes. No obvious CPU spike on frontends.
li: pinging runtime infra — I'm seeing elevated connection resets between proxy and model-serving pool. Also noticing a LOT fewer log lines from the runtime this window compared to normal traffic. Might be sampling change? (cc @arjun)
arjun: interesting — we rolled a sampling config tweak in obs-config yesterday to reduce ingestion. Could be that. Which logs are missing? request-level traces or engine-level KV cache logs?
maya: missing detailed engine logs (kv cache hits/misses), but proxy access logs are present. Hard to correlate without those runtime lines.
erin: posting the recent config rollout event: 
```
# rollout summary
obs-config sampling: from 100% -> 10% for runtime: 2026-03-13T14:05 UTC
k8s rollout: obs-config v3.4.1 -> v3.4.2
who: ops-automation
```
sam: if sampling was turned down, that would reduce log volume — but shouldn't cause 5xxs. Could be correlated: reduced KV cache visibility -> bad hypothesis hunting. We need timeline & raw runtime logs for the window 21:10-21:30.
maya: building timeline. Draft:
- 21:10: alert threshold crossed in proxy metrics
- 21:11: first customer report
- 21:12: incident bot paged
- 21:14: observed connection resets between proxy and runtime
- 21:18: partial runtime autoscaler activity noted
- 21:25: manual mitigation attempt (drain + restart) by li

li: mitigation I ran at ~21:25: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime-pool-usw2` for two affected node groups. After restart error-rate dropped but returned to ~4%.
dawn: sharing ad-hoc query for raw runtime logs (CloudLogs):
```
resource.type="k8s_container" AND log_name="runtime" AND timestamp >= "2026-03-14T21:05:00Z" AND timestamp < "2026-03-14T21:35:00Z" AND jsonPayload.request_id : "req_20260314_"
| limit 500
```
(Use project: redwood-obsv-prod)
maya: ran that query, only ~120 lines returned in that 30m window. Expecting ~2k lines. Clearly sampling/ingest reduced coverage. We need full packet to reconstruct timeline.
arjun: can someone run `kubectl get configmap obs-sampling -o yaml -n infra` and paste? Also check S3 raw logs retention/ingest pipeline throttling.
li: pasted configmap snippet:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: obs-sampling
data:
  runtime_sampling_ratio: "0.10"
  proxy_sampling_ratio: "1.0"
```
li: runtime_sampling_ratio was explicitly set to 0.10 yesterday. That matches the reduced lines. Ops automation applied it — likely intended to control costs but we lost critical fidelity for this oncall window.
erin: ops-bot confirms the automation job at 2026-03-13T14:05:23Z set runtime_sampling_ratio:0.10. Reverting to 1.0 would be a quick mitigation but might spike ingest costs.
maya: immediate mitigation proposal: revert runtime sampling to 1.0 for the next 60m, re-run the tail query, collect full logs, then roll forward with targeted sampling for non-production clusters. Who can revert now?
sam: I can do the revert. Steps:
1) kubectl apply -f obs-sampling-revert.yaml -n infra
2) restart obs-ingest pods: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/obs-ingest -n infra`
3) watch log count for runtime over next 10m

maya: go for it @sam. Notify customers if we expect partial recovery window.
sam: doing step 1 -> applied. Step 2 -> restarting obs-ingest pods now. Monitoring.
ops-bot: rollout status: obs-ingest rollout complete at 2026-03-14T21:37:10Z
sam: after revert, runtime logs in that window now show ~2.1k lines for 21:05-21:35. Pasting the relevant error pattern snippet (truncated):
```
2026-03-14T21:12:37Z runtime[pod-7] ERROR: kvcache write failed: errno=28; disk full? write returned EIO
2026-03-14T21:12:38Z runtime[pod-7] WARN: fallback path invoked: sync disabled
2026-03-14T21:12:39Z runtime[pod-9] ERROR: connection reset by peer while writing response
```
li: key callout — `errno=28` indicates disk full on some runtime nodes. The autoscaler churn may have launched nodes without proper EBS mount sizing? Checking PV metrics.
arjun: also seeing increased 95th latency in model inference around same time which could be explained by heavy disk I/O failure causing worker threads to block.
erin: running PV inspect and storage metrics now. Meanwhile, customer-facing: should we post an interim status in status.redwood.ai saying "Partial degradation with increased errors for text generation in US-WEST-2; mitigation underway"? We'll need communications consent.
maya: yes post that. I'll draft and send to comms for approval. (cc @erin)
sam: PV check: two pods had rootfs at 95% and IO error spikes. Crash loops started on a subset of pods 21:11-21:15. Looks like a misconfigured init job consumed temp disk. Searching deploy history...
li: found last init job change in runtime image v5.12.3 which added a local cache warmup step writing to /tmp/cache. The warmup assumed ephemeral SSD of 50GB but some node types are 20GB.
maya: that explains the errno=28. Hypothesis chain:
1) new warmup writes filled local disk on smaller nodes
2) kernel started returning EIO on writes -> kvcache writes failed -> runtime hit error paths -> proxy saw 502/504
3) autoscaler reacted and restarted nodes -> further instability

arjun: agree. Secondary observability gap: because sampling was 0.10 we couldn't see the early warmup log lines, slowing detection.
dawn: proposed post-incident mitigation list:
- patch runtime image to write to ephemeral path sized per node type OR skip warmup on small instances
- add pre-deploy check in CI: validate init job disk usage vs node flavor
- revert global sampling changes into gradual rollout with canary for observability-critical logs
- add alert: disk usage > 80% on runtime nodes triggers immediate page
erin: immediate next steps executed:
- sam applied revert to sampling (done)
- li rolled a patch to disable warmup on small nodes (hotfix) and rolled on 3 affected node groups (21:55)
- maya posted interim status update at 21:45

maya: current status (22:02): error rate back down to 0.6% (baseline ~0.2%). Customers experiencing low impact now but some request retries persisted until 21:58. We'll keep P1 open until 23:00 or until stability for 1h.
sam: collecting artifacts for RCA: pod logs (s3://redwood-incident-logs/1892504321/), config diffs, k8s events. I'll upload to the incident ticket.
arjun: I'll prepare a short writeup for the root cause and the observability gap (sampling change) and recommended guardrails.
maya: good thread. Two actions for oncall handoff: 1) leave P1 open; 2) next oncall (dawn) will validate post-recovery metrics and coordinate postmortem. @dawn you can take if OK.
dawn: taking handoff. I'll validate metric windows 22:00-23:00 and start the incident doc skeleton. Will include timeline + query snippets. Thanks team.
ops-bot: reminder scheduled: Create incident postmortem document in /incidents/1892504321-postmortem within 48h."
